# 

# 1\. LAB OVERVIEW

## 1.1  Why This Lab Exists

A monitor is a query plus a time window, a threshold and a message. Most noisy or silent alerts come from the query: the wrong aggregation, a missing scope, or a window that does not match how the data behaves. Composite monitors combine existing monitors with boolean logic — "backend errors AND CreditCardCheckError500 logged" routes to the payments team, "backend errors AND NOT CreditCardCheckError500" routes to the backend on-call — so that one symptom produces the right page instead of several confusing ones.  
In this lab you write a metric monitor query for the easyTravel backend error rate and a log monitor query for CreditCardCheckError500, validate them in the monitor editor, create them in the UI, combine them into two composite monitors, and then predict and verify every monitor state while the instructor switches the fault on and off.

| 🎯  NIIT iRUN Alignment |
| :---- |
| INCIDENT OWNERSHIP: Your monitors page the right team for the right reason. |
|  |
| TROUBLESHOOTING EXCELLENCE: You will use composite logic to separate causes that share the same symptom. |
|  |
| OPERATIONAL READINESS: Monitors are validated, created in the UI, tested with faults and cleaned up. |

## 1.3  Conceptual Foundation

Every Datadog monitor type has its own query form. They share the same idea: data query \+ evaluation window \+ comparison \+ threshold.  
*Figure: Monitor Query Anatomy — time\_aggr(time\_window) : space\_aggr : metric{scope} \[by {group}\] operator threshold · logs("search").index("\*").rollup("count").last("5m") \> N · Composite: A && \!B*

| Monitor Type | Query Form | Example (this lab) | Evaluates |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Metric ("query alert") | avg(last\_5m):p95:metric{scope} \> X | sum(last\_5m):errors / hits \* 100 \> 5 | Metric values over the window |
| Log ("log alert") | logs("query").index("\*").rollup("count").last("5m") \> N | logs("service:easytravel-backend env:cohort \\"CreditCardCheckError500\\"")… \> 10 | Count of matching logs |
| Composite | \<id\> && \<id\>, \|\|, \! | A && B · A && \!B | States of other monitors |
| APM ("query alert" / "trace-analytics alert") | Trace metrics or span search counts | (extension) | Spans / trace metrics |

*Figure: Composite Truth Table — A (backend error rate high) × B (CreditCardCheckError500 logged): A && B \= known credit-card fault → payments / commerce · A && \!B \= errors from something else → backend on-call · Composite Notifies Only When Its Expression Is True*

## 1.4  Learning Objectives

* Write metric and log monitor queries with correct aggregation, scope, window and threshold  
* Validate monitor queries in the monitor editor before saving them  
* Create metric, log and composite monitors in the UI and read their states on the Monitors pages  
* Build composite monitors with AND and NOT logic  
* Predict and verify monitor and composite states during different faults  
* Clean up monitors in the correct order

# 3\. CONCEPT DEEP-DIVE BEFORE STARTING

## 3.1  From Query to Monitor Query

A graph query becomes a monitor query by adding a time aggregation over an evaluation window and a comparison with a threshold: the error-ratio graph from Lab 4 becomes sum(last\_5m):…errors / …hits \* 100 \> 5\. Log monitors wrap a log search: logs("…").index("\*").rollup("count").last("5m") \> 10\. The options set warning/critical thresholds, how missing data is treated and whether a full window is required. Validating the query in the monitor editor catches syntax errors before anyone relies on the monitor.

| 💡  Why This Matters Operationally |
| :---- |
| Composite monitors encode diagnosis: they turn "two alerts at once" into one alert that already says which cause is likely. |
|  |
| Monitor definitions can be exported as JSON, reviewed, versioned and recreated — in this lab you create and delete them in the UI, with your seat prefix. |

## 3.2  The Critical Distinction: Component Monitors vs Composite Notifications

A composite monitor has no query of its own; it evaluates the states of its component monitors with &&, \|\| and \! and alerts only when the whole expression is true. Typically the components are kept silent (no @-notifications, used for state only) and only the composites notify the right team. A composite with NOT (A && \!B) is powerful but must be tested: when B recovers before A, the composite can change state.

| ⚠️  Most Common Mistake With Monitor Queries |
| :---- |
| A monitor uses avg(last\_1m):avg:…{\*} \> 1 for latency — it fires on single slow seconds at night and misses a booking outage hidden in the all-requests average by day. |
|  |
| REASON: The window is too short, the aggregation is the average, and the scope is everything. |
|  |
| YOU MUST pick the signal that matches the user experience (error ratio for failures, a percentile for slowness), scope to the service, use a window that smooths noise (5 minutes), and test with a real fault. |

## 3.3  Predicting Composite States

| Situation | A: backend error rate \> 5 % | B: CreditCardCheckError500 logs \> 10 | A && B  ·  A && \!B |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Healthy (none) | OK | OK | OK · OK |
| Other backend error (reasoning only) | ALERT | OK | OK · ALERT |
| CreditCardCheckError500 ON | ALERT | ALERT | ALERT · OK |
| Recovery | OK (after window) | OK (after window) | OK · may briefly ALERT if B clears before A |

| 📝  How to Decide the Window and Threshold |
| :---- |
| Ask: "What does normal look like, how fast must we know, and how noisy is the signal?" Use the Lab 4 graphs: the backend error ratio is close to 0 % when healthy and clearly above it during the fault, so 5 % (critical) over 5 minutes separates them clearly (the Day 2 shared monitor uses the same threshold). CreditCardCheckError500 lines are absent when healthy and frequent during the fault, so \> 10 in 5 minutes is safe. |

# 6\. TROUBLESHOOTING — COMMON ISSUES & FIXES

| Issue / Error | Cause | Diagnosis | Fix |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Cannot save a monitor (permission error) | Your Datadog role lacks Monitors Write, or a required name/tag is missing | Read the red error banner in the editor | Tell your instructor; never use API keys in this lab |
| Editor shows "query is invalid" for monitor A | Metric name or tag wrong, or the formula is incomplete | Graph the same query in Metrics Explorer | Copy the metric names and tags shown in Metrics Summary; check both parts of the ratio |
| Monitor stays "No Data" | Query scope matches no data | Remove one tag at a time in Metrics Explorer | Fix the scope; notify\_no\_data is false so it will not page |
| Composite creation fails | Component monitor not saved yet, or the wrong monitor selected | Manage Monitors: check that A and B exist | Save A and B first, then select them in the composite editor |
| Delete fails for A or B | Still used by a composite | Error message names the composite | Delete C1 and C2 first |
| States change slower than expected | Evaluation delay and 5-minute windows | Status & History on the monitor page | Wait 2–3 more minutes; ask the instructor for the last fault cue |

# 

# 7\. INSTRUCTOR DEBRIEF — 7 MINUTES

## 7.1  Discussion Questions

| Discussion 1 — Query to Monitor |
| :---- |
| Without notes: turn "backend error rate" into a monitor query with a 5-minute window and a 5 % threshold. |
| What would change for a 99 % availability SLO? |
|  |
| Key answer to explore: sum(last\_5m):errors / hits \* 100 \> 5; for SLOs use longer windows or SLO monitors. |
| **Discussion 2 — Composite Logic** |
| Which page would have reached the right team faster: A alone, or the composites? |
| When is OR (\|\|) useful in a composite? |
|  |
| Key insight: composites encode diagnosis; OR combines several symptoms of one problem. |
| **Discussion 3 — Recovery Effects** |
| Why can A && \!B alert briefly during recovery from the fault? |
| How would you avoid that (windows, recovery thresholds, renotify settings)? |
|  |
| Key answer: B clears before A; align windows or add recovery thresholds and delays. |
| **Discussion 4 — Monitors as Code** |
| What does the monitor JSON export give you that clicking in the UI does not? |
| Where would you store these definitions in a real team (Terraform, Git)? |
|  |
| Answer: review, repeatability and clean-up; store in Git and apply with Terraform or CI. |

## 7.2  Common Mistakes — Learn From These

| Mistake | Why It Happens | Consequence | Prevention |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| No time window in the query | Copying a graph query | Validation error | time\_aggr(last\_5m): prefix |
| Averages for latency monitors | Default aggregation | Missed slow tails | Percentiles on distributions |
| Notifying from every component | Wanting all alerts | Duplicate pages | Components silent, composites notify |
| Untested composites | Logic "looks right" | Wrong team paged | Predict, then test with the fault |
| Untagged monitors | Speed | Hard to find, never cleaned up | Always tag (lab:day3, service, env) |

# 10\. QUICK REFERENCE — DATADOG MONITOR QUERIES & COMPOSITES COMMAND CARD

Bookmark this page. Every command you need in SOP order.

| Category | Command | Purpose |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Metric monitor | sum(last\_5m):errors / hits \* 100 \> 5 | type "query alert" |
| Log monitor | logs("q").index("\*").rollup("count").last("5m") \> 10 | type "log alert" |
| Composite | "\<A\> && \<B\>"  ·  "\<A\> && \!\<B\>"  ·  \|\| | type "composite" |
| Thresholds | options.thresholds {critical, warning} | Must match the query |
| Validate | Editor preview \+ Source (\</\>) toggle | Graph draws, no red banner |
| Create | Create button; ID in the URL | Keep the ID |
| List by tag | Manage Monitors → filter tag:lab:day3 tag:u\<seat\> | Status per monitor |
| Delete | Select → Delete | Composites first |
| Naming | Seat prefix \[u\<seat\>\] in every name and tag | No API keys needed |
| Window | last\_5m smooths noise | Detection vs noise |
| No data | notify\_no\_data: false | Avoid pages on gaps |
| States | OK · Warn · Alert · No Data | Status & History |
